newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends firmer at fresh one-year high.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends firmer at fresh one-year high.

text.p: COMEX copper settled firmer with the most active July contract hitting a fresh one-year high of 120.00 cents as the market shrugged off news that Kennecott's large smelter was back on stream, dealers said.
Copper prices are now back to pre-Sumitomo June 1996 crash levels.
The gains in copper came amid some liquidation of positions held by Cerro Sales Corp, the New York trading house being taken over by a subsidiary of Germany's Metallgesellschaft, floor sources said.
Arbitrage and COMEX spreads were being affected by the liquidation because both Cerro and MG are hit arbitrage dealers, floor sources added.
John Tyree of FIMAT futures said the advance came from some fund buying and then the market largely traded sideways.
"We have made a new high and the trend is up. My only concern is that we are technically somewhat overbought," Tyree said.
COMEX July copper settled 1.05 cents firmer at 119.45 cents per pound, traded 120.00 to 117.80 cents. Volume was estimated at 10,000 lots.
The gains came despite a series of more modest declines in LME stocks, and sharply rising COMEX stocks. LME stocks fell 450 tonnes Wednesday to 136,575 tonnes.
The LME backwardation widened slightly Wednesday before ending at $74/$78.
Kennecott said its 310,000 short tons per year copper smelter in Utah restarted Tuesday after a 42-day shutdown for maintenance.
The U.S. market has been fairly tight for some time, partly due to Kennecott's outage, but the company said the smelter will not reach full capacity until later this year.
Late Tuesday supervisors at Chile Copper Co's huge Chuquicamata mine accepted a company pay offer, removing a potential strike and price prop from the red metal market.
